event.hazel_heart2.0.text: Shh. Back here, behind Natural History. (Nobody comes this far. That's the point.)
event.hazel_heart2.0.why: she leads the player into her hiding place, not to an object

event.hazel_heart2.1.text: A snowdrop, pressed in an almanac eighty-one years ago. Page two hundred and four.
event.hazel_heart2.1.why: precise numbers instead of 'a hundred years'

event.hazel_heart2.2.text: This is the reading nook. One chair. (I've never needed two.)
event.hazel_heart2.2.why: reveals the nook and seeds the second chair

event.hazel_heart5.0.text: I wrote you something. (Five drafts. Four are on the floor.)

event.hazel_heart5.1.text: It's a small poem. Six lines. If you laugh, laugh at line four. It's the weak one.
event.hazel_heart5.1.why: deflects fear onto a line number

event.hazel_heart5.2.text: You read to the end. (I watched.) Nobody's done that before.
event.hazel_heart5.2.why: the real thank-you, as an observation

event.reading_night.1.text: (It doesn't.) I brought something. It's in my sleeve. I haven't decided if it comes out.
event.reading_night.1.why: teases Ione back and makes the poem a physical secret

dlg.reading.hazel.0.text: (Nobody has to hear it.) What would you do? ...If you were me, I mean.

dlg.reading.hazel.c2.text: Listen first. Ione's face needs the practice.

dlg.reading.hazel.r0.text: (Fine.) A short one. Eleven lines. (I counted twice. It's still eleven.)

dlg.reading.hazel.r1.text: Someone else's, then. Kinder to the room. (Mine stays in my sleeve.)

dlg.reading.hazel.r2.text: Ione first. (Thank you.) I'm not leaving. I'm only sitting very still.
dlg.reading.hazel.r2.why: relief, and a promise to stay

event.reading_night.poem.text: The lamp does not mind the dark. It keeps it company. ...That's the last of the eleven. (The rest were warming up.)
event.reading_night.poem.why: reconciles the eleven lines with the two we hear

event.reading_night.borrowed.text: Ione reads two pages about the winter sea. Hazel turns toward the lamp and stays very still.

event.reading_night.listen.text: Ione reads first, an old page about birds in fall. Hazel says nothing, and does not leave.

event.festival_winter_lanterns.1.text: One lantern, one wish. Please keep yours folded up. (Last winter four people said theirs aloud.)
event.festival_winter_lanterns.1.why: a count of other people's wishes, setting up Felix

event.hazel_heart4.intro.text: I'd like to swap something. A book for a book. (Or a book for anything.) Is that odd?
event.hazel_heart4.intro.why: opens the door wider than she means to

dlg.hazel.swap.0.text: What would you lend me? (I'm not choosing for you. I'm leaning slightly.)
dlg.hazel.swap.0.why: the aside admits she has a hope

dlg.hazel.swap.c1.text: A recipe card, if that counts.

dlg.hazel.swap.r0.text: Oh. (It's a both-hands book.) I'll read it twice. Once for the story, once for you.

dlg.hazel.swap.r1.text: A recipe. (A book without a spine.) I'll shelve it under Fiction until I bake it.

dlg.hazel.swap.r2.text: Thank you for saying so. (Most people pretend.) I'll find something short. There's a heron in it.

event.hazel_heart4.after.text: I'll look after it. (I always do.) Return date: whenever. I've never written that before.
event.hazel_heart4.after.why: trust shown as a broken rule

event.hazel_heart6.intro.text: Could you come to the back? Past Geography. (I'm not hiding. I'm shelving very slowly.)

dlg.hazel.hiding.0.text: The festival wants someone to read aloud. Ione said my name. (I've been back here since ten.) Is that strange?
dlg.hazel.hiding.0.why: names the heart 6 trigger from her bible

dlg.hazel.hiding.c0.text: Ask what she hears back here.

dlg.hazel.hiding.c2.text: Joke that she could hide in a book.

dlg.hazel.hiding.r0.text: Pages turning, two rooms away. Other people's thoughts, kept. (It never asks me to read aloud.)
dlg.hazel.hiding.r0.why: the quiet as company that makes no demands

dlg.hazel.hiding.r1.text: ...Oh. (Nobody's ever sat down. They usually say 'there you are'.)

dlg.hazel.hiding.r2.text: Ha. (A small one.) I tried that once. The book was too thin.

event.hazel_heart6.after.text: I checked your face just now. It stayed kind. (I'll think about the festival. Slowly.)

dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r0.text: Lovely. (I'm going to press that word in a book.) Thank you.

dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r1.text: The middle. (I knew it. Lines five through eight.) Thank you for saying it out loud.

dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r2.text: The lamp is a bit much. (It's meant to be.) It stays. It's my only regular listener.

event.hazel_heart8.intro.text: Would you hear a thing I wrote? (Just you. I rehearsed on the cat. It left.)

event.hazel_heart8.after.text: One day I'll read it properly. To more than one. (Two, perhaps. Let's not be reckless.)

event.hazel_heart10.intro.text: I'll read it for you. Just you. (The shelves don't count. They've heard it already.)
event.hazel_heart10.intro.why: keeps the shipped promise, adds rehearsal history

event.hazel_heart10.outro.text: {if choice:hazel.rehearsal.critique}I cut the middle. (You were right. It breathes now.) Did you hear the new line? It's about you.{else}I kept the lamp. (And I added you.) Did you hear? Third line from the end.{/if}
event.hazel_heart10.outro.why: the surprise: a line about the player

event.hazel_friend.ask.text: Do you have blackberries? (A book is overdue by forty-one years. I'm baking an apology.)

event.hazel_friend.fallback.text: Come back with blackberries? (It's a small crisis. A quiet one. It has waited forty-one years.)

event.hazel_friend.success.text: Perfect. A tart, then a knock on his door. (He may not forgive the library. He'll eat.)

event.hazel_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. (I wasn't going to say. Ione told the cake.) It's very small. Please sit.
event.hazel_birthday.intro.why: Ione as accomplice, cake as witness

dlg.hazel.birthday.r0.text: Two words, said kindly. (I counted. I always count.) I'll keep them.

dlg.hazel.birthday.r1.text: That one. (You remembered.) I need a moment. The lighthouse keeper would understand.

dlg.hazel.birthday.r2.text: (Nobody is singing.) This is the best present. Please stay until the cake is gone.
dlg.hazel.birthday.r2.why: distinct from the heart 6 silence reply

event.hazel_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.hazel.wish}Two kind words. I wrote them in the margin of today.{else}{if choice:bday.hazel.read}My favorite line, aloud. I've never heard it in another voice. It sounds truer.{else}A shared silence. The quietest birthday I've had. (Next year, again, please.){/if}{/if}

adds.text: Someone wrote the first frost beside it, in pencil. They were three days early.
Here. A fresh one, for you. (Please don't press it in a cookbook.)
Read it to yourself. Please. (Not aloud. I'm not there yet.)
adds.why: her fear of reading aloud, stated as a request

adds.text: Blackberry jam. Two jars. A bribe, for your silence about line four.
adds.why: voices the jam gift, ends on a joke

threads.hazel_heart2: The nook has one chair; will there ever be two?
threads.hazel_heart5: Line four, and whether she will ever read a poem aloud.
threads.reading_night: The poem stayed in her sleeve (or was eleven lines with only two heard): what are the other nine?
threads.hazel_heart4: Which book with a heron in it she will lend back.
threads.hazel_heart6: Will she read at the festival?
threads.hazel_heart8: Who the second listener will be.
threads.hazel_heart10: A line in her poem is about the player; when will anyone else hear it?
threads.hazel_friend: Who borrowed a book forty-one years ago, and why did he never return it?
threads.hazel_birthday: Next year's birthday: she has asked for it again.

notes: hazel_heart10 cues music hazel_theme, which is not in the music cue list; it will play silent.
hazel_heart10 plays sfx coin during the reading; pageturn would fit better.
hazel_birthday r0 said 'four words' for a birthday wish; changed to two and matched the after-branch.
